digest.component_or_area: code-review criterion / CI gate compatibility verifier
propositions: New hard-fail CI gates/floors/caps without grandfather/if-present guards cause in-flight branches created before the gate change to fail unexpectedly.

A project-owned advisory code-review criterion `project.ci-gate-compat` must detect pipeline/gate-configuration changes that introduce hard-fail steps or required gates lacking if-present/grandfather protection.

The criterion must be triggered declaratively via glob patterns matching CI configuration files across multiple CI vendors (GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines, Buildkite, Bitbucket, Drone), without hard-coding CI-vendor-specific logic in Python.
The glob set must be project-overridable via a `[code_review] ci_config_globs` config key so projects can declare unusual pipeline locations without editing rebar code.

Activated project criteria must be filtered by their effective `applies_to` globs against the review's changed files before dispatch, while empty `applies_to` retains the always-on behavior for existing criteria.

The criterion ships as advisory (non-blocking, calibrated on real reviews) with rubric phrased in CI-agnostic language avoiding vendor names, paired with twelve balanced evaluation cases (6 fire, 6 pass) achieving perfect recall and zero false accept.
